content: Hydroxyzine is a medication primarily used for the short-term management of nervousness and tension associated with certain mental or mood disorders, such as anxiety or dementia. It is also utilized to alleviate withdrawal symptoms, including anxiety and agitation, in individuals recovering from alcohol dependence. This drug belongs to the class of medications known as antihistamines. Its mechanism of action is thought to involve modulation of specific natural substances in the body, such as acetylcholine and serotonin, or direct effects on certain areas of the brain. Hydroxyzine is administered via intramuscular injection as directed by a healthcare provider. If you are instructed to self-administer this medication at home, it is essential to receive thorough training on preparation and usage from a healthcare professional. Before use, inspect the solution for any particles or discoloration; if either is present, the medication should not be used. Common side effects of hydroxyzine include drowsiness, dizziness, blurred vision, dry mouth, constipation, and headache. It is important to note that this medication has been prescribed because the potential benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to hydroxyzine are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. In the United States, patients should contact their doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, patients should also consult their doctor for guidance. Before using hydroxyzine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, cetirizine, or levocetirizine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Hydroxyzine may cause a condition known as QT prolongation, which affects the heart's rhythm. The risk of QT prolongation may be heightened if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other medications that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can also increase the risk of QT prolongation, particularly if you are using certain drugs (e.g., diuretics) or experiencing conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This medication may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or blurred vision. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness or clear vision until you are confident you can perform them safely. Limit the consumption of alcoholic beverages. Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of hydroxyzine, particularly drowsiness, confusion, constipation, difficulty urinating, or QT prolongation. Children may also be more susceptible to the drug's side effects. During pregnancy, hydroxyzine should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this medication passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of hydroxyzine or increase the risk of serious side effects. It is crucial to maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Check the labels of all your medications, especially allergy or cough-and-cold products, as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. Hydroxyzine may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as allergy skin tests or urine corticosteroid tests, potentially leading to false results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If you miss a dose of hydroxyzine, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. It is important to adhere to the prescribed schedule for this medication. Store hydroxyzine at room temperature, away from light. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
